newsitem.title: USA: Fannie Mae exceeds housing goals in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae exceeds housing goals in 1996.

text.p: Federal National Mortgage Association said its financing activity surpassed all of the housing goals set by regulators in 1996.
Fannie Mae, the nation's largest source of funds for home mortgages, said that more than 45 percent of the units it financed in 1996 were for low- and moderate-income households.
"Fannie Mae had another year of record-setting accomplishments through our low- and moderate-income financing," said James Johnson, Fannie Mae chairman and chief executive officer.
Fannie Mae's stock gained 1-1/4 to 38-1/4 and was one of the most active issues on the New York Stock Exchange.
Underserved areas accounted for 28 percent of Fannie Mae's business, exceeding the regulatory goal of 21 percent.

Low- and moderate-income households, those with incomes less than or equal to 100 percent of an area's median, represented over 45 percent of Fannie Mae's business, compared with a goal of 40 percent, the company said.

Special affordable housing (low- and very low-income households living in both single-family and multifamily residences) represented 17 percent of the company's business in 1996, exceeding the one-year goal of 12 percent, the company said.
Fannie Mae said it financed $2.3 billion in multifamily special affordable mortgages in 1996 against a minimum goal of $1.3 billion.
Congressionally chartered Fannie Mae has committed to purchase $1 trillion in "targeted lending" for 10 million homes by the end of the decade.
The "targeted lending" will serve both low- and moderate-income families, minorities, residents of central cities and other underserved areas, and people who have special housing needs.
